title: Anthropic’s IPO puts AI’s circular financing boom to the test
lede: Anthropic's IPO tests the circular deals behind the AI boom: Amazon and Google, two of its biggest suppliers, also hold stakes worth about $308 billion at the $83 offer price.

points: Per the prospectus, Amazon's 14.7% stake is worth about $159 billion and Google's 13.7% stake nearly $149 billion.
Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft, Broadcom, Micron and TSMC joined Google in a $26 billion private placement, and most also sell Anthropic compute under multibillion-dollar deals.
Anthropic expects about $220 billion in cash and short-term investments after listing, against $900 billion in commitments, mostly compute.
It booked $17 billion in third-quarter 2026 revenue; a SemiAnalysis analyst says covering its compute needs roughly $280 billion over four years, which he calls achievable.
Both analysts quoted see losing the frontier race as the main risk, while cloud suppliers profit whichever model wins.

sections.text: Once public money replaces supplier money, Anthropic's compute deals stand on its own revenue; analysts expect cloud capacity to keep growing whichever lab's models developers pick.
